requirements.title: Budgets, deterministic cancellation and process ownership
Legacy correspondence and no shell execution

cases.name: Static/local mode detection
preconditions: Target implementation built from the pinned specification revision.
Fixtures and fault controls named by the case are available and hashed.
steps: Open hosted reader; launch with omitted profile on Windows and WSL, launch each valid explicit profile, reject invalid OS/profile pairs, and query health/runtime with and without credentials.
expected: Static has disabled live actions and makes no API request; local binds only 127.0.0.1:8765; omission selects the OS profile matching the running environment's Torch build and a mismatching explicit profile fails with BACKEND_VERSION_MISMATCH; a CUDA profile starts only after a passing preflight, win-cuda only on native Windows and wsl-cuda only on WSL; profile is instance-immutable with no fallback; health is minimal; runtime/status/P00 fields match the selected profile.

cases.name: Fixed service-worker boundary
preconditions: Target implementation built from the pinned specification revision.
Fixtures and fault controls named by the case are available and hashed.
steps: Submit one fixture for every operation while recording service imports, child argv/environment and dispatch.
Submit command, module, URL and uploaded-code fields.
expected: Service process imports no ML backend; every job uses fixed isolated worker and allowlisted environment; unknown/code-bearing inputs fail before spawn.

cases.name: Pairing, origin and expiry
preconditions: Target implementation built from the pinned specification revision.
Fixtures and fault controls named by the case are available and hashed.
steps: Exercise valid, expired and reused 120-second bootstrap; idle and absolute test clocks; hostile Host, Origin, preflight, missing bearer and CSRF; reload same tab.

Send each boundary-order fixture: wrong Host; OPTIONS with hostile Origin; mutation without Origin; mutation with Origin http://evil.example; GET with Sec-Fetch-Site cross-site; GET without Sec-Fetch-Site; mutation without Authorization; expired session; mutation without X-LLMF-CSRF; wrong Content-Type; oversize body. Each fixture also violates every later check.
Revoke a session with DELETE /api/v1/sessions/current and reuse its tokens; run connect twice and exchange the first secret; open 33 sessions.
expected: Only one valid exchange succeeds; hostile requests fail before body parse; credentials persist only sessionStorage; two-hour idle, 12-hour absolute and restart invalidate exactly as specified.

Statuses in order: 403 ORIGIN_REJECTED/HOST_MISMATCH, 403/PREFLIGHT_REJECTED, 403/ORIGIN_MISSING, 403/ORIGIN_MISMATCH, 403/FETCH_SITE_REJECTED, 403/FETCH_SITE_REJECTED, 401 AUTH_REQUIRED, 401 SESSION_EXPIRED, 403 CSRF_REJECTED, 415 UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE, 413 PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE; the first failing check decides and no body is parsed.
Revoked tokens return 401 AUTH_REQUIRED; the superseded bootstrap secret returns 401 AUTH_REQUIRED; the 33rd exchange returns 409 REGISTRY_LIMIT reason SESSION_LIMIT.

cases.name: Storage traversal and atomic commit
preconditions: Target implementation built from the pinned specification revision.
Fixtures and fault controls named by the case are available and hashed.
steps: Use symlink/weak-permission roots; path, link, duplicate, sparse, bomb and traversal archives; inject failure before rename and before metadata commit.
expected: Unsafe roots/members are rejected; no write escapes root; no metadata points to partial bytes; committed bytes remain immutable and digest-addressed.

cases.name: Every request boundary
preconditions: Target implementation built from the pinned specification revision.
Fixtures and fault controls named by the case are available and hashed.
steps: For JSON, dataset, bundle, record, UTF-8, prompt and chat limits submit exact-limit and limit-plus-one fixtures plus duplicate-key/nonfinite/trailing JSON.
expected: Exact limits are accepted when otherwise valid; plus-one and malformed inputs return the frozen code/status and create no job or dataset.

cases.name: Registry pagination and uploads
preconditions: Target implementation built from the pinned specification revision.
Fixtures and fault controls named by the case are available and hashed.
steps: Import a valid three-part dataset and a bad final part; page tied records with limit 1; reuse cursor with changed filter; stage an inert bundle.

Create/update/conflict/read progress; create/update/list/delete-preview/delete notes and conversations; append a turn through commit-generation; create/verify/assess evidence; preview/apply v1 and v2 progress; create capstone attempt; export selected backup.

Read startup preflight; commit a completed conversation generation atomically; reject partial generation; export a conversation dataset candidate; inspect capstone creation response versus later detail.
Fail a tiny_train after two checkpoint commits; list GET /artifacts?job_id and GET /runs?job_state=failed; read log_artifact_ids.stdout content.

Export backups with include_notes true and no note_ids, with note_ids [N1, N2], with include_notes false and note_ids [N1], with note_ids [], with a deleted note ID, and with include_conversations true and confirm_sensitive_text false.
expected: Dataset commit is all-or-nothing; ordering/cursor has no gaps or duplicates; changed cursor fails; staging asserts transport safety only.

Every learner action has one callable closed-schema endpoint; revision conflicts do not mutate; delete requires fresh confirmed preview and tombstones content; migration preview is nonmutating and apply is atomic; sealed token and backup exclude credentials.

Preflight exposes fixed checks without host paths; generation commits user+assistant or neither; exported conversation cannot train before dataset audit; release token appears once and detail retains freeze/exposure without secret.
Both checkpoints, the metrics artifact to the last boundary and both logs are listed with job_id set; the run appears under job_state=failed; logs download as untrusted text.

The first export holds every live note and the second exactly N1 and N2; the others return 400 VALIDATION_FAILED with SEMANTIC_INVALID at /note_ids, SEMANTIC_INVALID at /note_ids, REFERENCE_MISSING at /note_ids/<index> and SEMANTIC_INVALID at /confirm_sensitive_text, creating no artifact.

cases.name: Idempotent job creation and disk reserve
preconditions: Target implementation built from the pinned specification revision.
Fixtures and fault controls named by the case are available and hashed.
steps: Submit identical and changed bodies under one key; expire session and replay; mock available bytes at estimate+1GiB and one byte below for each estimate class.
Replay create, update, apply and delete mutations for learner-state endpoints with identical and changed idempotency bodies; fill each registry to its exact cap.

Submit with key K in session S1, lose the response, let S1 expire, pair S2 and query GET /jobs?idempotency_key=K and ?request_sha256; replay K with identical bytes in S2; replay K with changed bytes; replay a key whose first attempt returned 400; replay a multipart dataset upload with reordered parts.
Submit tiny_train with width/heads/layers giving P=9,999,220, steps 2000, eval_every 1 (estimate 257,032,031,712 bytes); then the same with eval_every 100.
With 4,990 checkpoint rows registered, submit tiny_train steps 50 eval_every 5 (Ck 12); with 4,988 rows submit steps 50 eval_every 10 (Ck 7).
Submit smollm2-capstone-lora-v1 with 20 updates and inspect the recorded reservation.
expected: Identical replay returns original; changed conflicts; exact reserve accepts; one-byte-below rejects without row/event.
All mutation replays are stable; changed body conflicts; next item at quota returns REGISTRY_LIMIT before row/bytes change.

Exactly one job exists and is found by both filters; the identical replay returns the stored response with header Idempotent-Replayed: true; changed bytes return 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT; the 4xx first attempt was not stored so the retry is evaluated fresh; reordered multipart parts with identical bytes replay.
The eval_every 1 request returns 400 VALIDATION_FAILED reason ESTIMATE_EXCEEDS_ROOT_QUOTA at eval_every on an empty root; eval_every 100 is accepted when free space allows.
Ck 12 against 10 remaining checkpoint rows returns 409 REGISTRY_LIMIT reason REGISTRY_COUNT_EXCEEDED before any row; Ck 7 is accepted and reserves 7 checkpoint and 57 artifact rows.
The capstone reservation uses Ck = 2 + ceil(20/5) = 6 and the 1 GiB floor.

cases.name: FIFO, ninth queued and transitions
preconditions: Target implementation built from the pinned specification revision.
Fixtures and fault controls named by the case are available and hashed.
steps: Block worker, enqueue eight jobs, submit ninth; cancel queued; drive completed, failed, interrupted paths; repeat cancel on all terminal states.

Validate against Job: queued with phase/step; cancelling with error; interrupted with terminal_reason completed; unstarted interrupted with a checkpoint; failed whose terminal_reason differs from error.code; interrupted with error OUT_OF_MEMORY.
Cancel a job in starting before spawn and after spawn before the running acknowledgment.
expected: One active/eight queued; ninth 429; FIFO stable; only declared transitions occur; terminal states never change.
Every listed record is rejected by the Job schema or JOB_FAILED_REASON; the service never emits one.

Before spawn: queued-cancel semantics (no worker, no checkpoint, interrupted/user_cancelled). After spawn: worker signalled, interrupted/user_cancelled within the 30-second grace, no checkpoint unless one was committed.

cases.name: Cancellation, deadline and unrelated process
preconditions: Target implementation built from the pinned specification revision.
Fixtures and fault controls named by the case are available and hashed.
steps: Run signed tiny-v2 diagnosis preset; observe step-25 checkpoint/hold, cancel, and separately let 10-minute clock expire; exercise 60-minute deadline and hard-stop grace; keep unrelated Python sentinel.
Submit the diagnosis hold with steps 10; with eval_every 10; with the weight-tied profile.
Request learner cancellation at 59:45 of the compute deadline; separately make ownership unprovable.
expected: Cancel yields interrupted step 25 checkpoint; hold expiry yields interrupted exercise_timeout and no later update; deadline uses 30-second grace; sentinel remains alive; no unowned PID is signaled.
Each hold variant returns 400 VALIDATION_FAILED reason DIAGNOSIS_HOLD_INVALID at curriculum_hold_after_step with no job row.

The late cancel keeps its full 30-second grace and ends interrupted/user_cancelled; unprovable ownership ends interrupted/worker_ownership_unknown with error WORKER_OWNERSHIP_UNKNOWN, no signal sent, and scheduling paused for the root.

cases.name: Restart recovery and reconnect
preconditions: Target implementation built from the pinned specification revision.
Fixtures and fault controls named by the case are available and hashed.
steps: Stop service with queued and running jobs, restart same root, pair again and reconcile cached IDs; inject database/digest corruption.
Stop the service cleanly (serve receives SIGINT/SIGTERM or Windows console close) with one running and two queued jobs; separately kill the service process.
expected: Queued keeps order; active becomes interrupted service_restarted; sessions invalidate; UI shows unknown until snapshot; corruption is read-only recovery with mutations blocked.
Clean stop: running job interrupted/service_shutdown before exit, queued jobs stay queued in FIFO order. Kill: running job interrupted/service_restarted at the next recovery.

cases.name: Bounded ordered event replay
preconditions: Target implementation built from the pinned specification revision.
Fixtures and fault controls named by the case are available and hashed.
steps: Produce maximum 2,001 metrics and checkpoints, 32 phases/warnings, 16 progress and terminal; page 500, reconnect SSE with duplicate cursor, then attempt one excess producer event.

Request events with after_cursor = last_cursor + 1; run a 2,000-update job and count persisted progress events and state_changed events; kill the service between a checkpoint file rename and its row commit, then recover.
expected: All at-most-4,096 events replay once in cursor order; heartbeat has no cursor; SSE closes at bounds; duplicate ignored; excess causes WORKER_PROTOCOL_ERROR without pruning prior events.

after_cursor beyond the log returns 400 VALIDATION_FAILED reason SEMANTIC_INVALID at after_cursor; at most 16 progress events at k/16 milestones plus terminal, never rewritten; at most five state_changed events on any path; the renamed-but-uncommitted checkpoint is an orphan and the latest durable checkpoint is the last committed row.

cases.name: All operation schemas and semantics
preconditions: Target implementation built from the pinned specification revision.
Fixtures and fault controls named by the case are available and hashed.
steps: Submit valid/min/max and one invalid field for each of 15 operations including both tokenizer profiles and context_preview; run both applied adapter presets, verify the frozen validation comparator, run paired sealed evaluation twice, and inspect tokenizer/weight/resume/evaluate/generate effects and artifacts.
Run standard and fixed weight-tied architecture profiles and reject any uploaded or arbitrary architecture code.

Create preview then send unchanged generation; independently recompute canonical_generation_request_sha256 and context_preview_digest from the exact field objects; alter each bound prompt/message/decoding/identity/device field and retry.

For every semantic-rules.json rule with a rejection, submit the boundary pair at the limit and one past it (the following pairs are mandatory in addition to the per-rule pairs: one chat message of 2,048 four-byte scalars = 8,192 bytes and one more scalar; 16,384-byte and 16,385-byte tiny prompts; export selections of 0, 1, 100 and 101 IDs; a resume selection without dataset bytes; a tiny-profile evaluation of an adapter).
expected: Closed schemas enforce bounds; tokenizer profile/type agree and tokenizer creates no weights; the capstone preset is seed 29 and exactly 20 updates; selection orders exact-intent numerator, schema-valid numerator, finite supervised-response mean NLL, then earliest step; inference/evaluation do not update; resume preserves lineage/optimizer/RNG; paired token is consumed once even on interruption.
Only internal architecture profile IDs execute; tokenizer/model/resume/generation semantics remain distinct.
Only unchanged request accepts preview; every altered or corrupt/missing preview is rejected pre-job as CONTEXT_PREVIEW_STALE; preview performs no weight load or inference.
At-limit requests are accepted; each past-limit request returns 400 VALIDATION_FAILED with the rule's reason_code and field_path and creates no job.

cases.name: CLI/API parity without shell
preconditions: Target implementation built from the pinned specification revision.
Fixtures and fault controls named by the case are available and hashed.
steps: Export request.json, submit through CLI and HTTP, compare canonical records; scan the companion package source and find no `shell=True`, `os.system`, `os.popen`, `eval(` or `exec(` call and no subprocess argument built from learner text; run legacy-equivalence fixture.

Run E01 harness with a nonexistent absolute output directory for exact edit, protected-byte change and one failing test; retry against an existing output path; inspect receipt/log atomicity, control-channel registration and tied training verification binding.
expected: CLI and API records match; learner text never becomes argv/shell; pure-mechanics equivalence fields meet absolute and relative tolerance 1e-6 (tokenizer IDs, shifted targets, parameter count and greedy token IDs exactly equal) while artifact formats stay distinct.

Exact edit atomically creates the output directory with receipt.json and bounded logs plus one hash-bound registered receipt; existing output exits 2 without mutation, protected diff exits 3, and failed test exits 4; tied training requires verification ID and labels the built-in matching backend without claiming learner source trained.

cases.name: Safe artifact serving
preconditions: Target implementation built from the pinned specification revision.
Fixtures and fault controls named by the case are available and hashed.
steps: Request a 1,024-byte allowlisted UTF-8 text artifact; 262,144-byte and 262,145-byte text artifacts; one HTML, one SVG, one .ipynb and one binary artifact; a Range request; an artifact whose display name is `..\x<script>.html`; and an artifact whose content is `<script>alert(1)</script>`.
expected: Only allowlisted text through 262,144 bytes previews; HTML, SVG, notebook, binary and the 262,145-byte text are sent with Content-Disposition attachment and nosniff; Range 416; UI renders text without markup execution.

cases.name: Backend/device/download exactness
preconditions: Target implementation built from the pinned specification revision.
Fixtures and fault controls named by the case are available and hashed.
steps: Remove/mismatch each backend; request CUDA per profile; replay exact manifest downloads and alter host/path/query/redirect/count/byte/digest; inject timeout, ENOSPC and OOM.
expected: Preflight reports exact capability/device failure with no fallback; only eight pinned files and redirects pass; any mismatch leaves no model; runtime faults never report success.

A redirect to another path or region under an allowed host succeeds when the bytes verify; each redirect mutation (a host outside the allowed suffixes, a third redirect, userinfo, a fragment, http or a port other than 443) ends model_prepare failed with job.error.code DOWNLOAD_SOURCE_REJECTED, retryable false, no model and no partial file; the error message names the host but not the query.

cases.name: Export, validate and clean-root import
preconditions: Target implementation built from the pinned specification revision.
Fixtures and fault controls named by the case are available and hashed.
steps: Export root A; stage in empty root B; validate then import under skip and copy; corrupt a member; evaluate/generate returned local model.
Export thin and full bundles with per-checkpoint resume-state choices and conversation selection.
expected: Validation is read-only; corrupt import registers nothing; skip/copy identity maps follow data contract; imported provenance remains imported; root B does not read A; reuse works via local IDs.
Thin is non-loadable and omits weights; full includes inference bytes and only explicitly selected resume state; sensitive conversation inclusion is previewed.

cases.name: Truthful post-accept faults
preconditions: Target implementation built from the pinned specification revision.
Fixtures and fault controls named by the case are available and hashed.
steps: Inject ENOSPC at artifact and SQLite phases, malformed worker messages, nonfinite metric, bad hash, step mismatch and unexpected exit zero/nonzero.
expected: Every accepted job ends in exactly one of completed, failed or interrupted, reached only along the 04-RUNTIME-AND-API.md state machine; committed evidence remains; partial output quarantines; no failed/interrupted path is labelled completed.

cases.name: Audit privacy and UI truth
preconditions: Target implementation built from the pinned specification revision.
Fixtures and fault controls named by the case are available and hashed.
steps: Submit prompts/messages/secrets and inspect HTTP headers, audit rows, five rotated logs and diagnostic exports; compare UI labels to event snapshots.
Preview then delete note/conversation and inspect tombstone audit.
expected: Logs/audit omit secrets/content/full bodies; request/entity metadata remains; diagnostics are opt-in; running/completed labels require persisted reconciled events.
Deleted content is absent while ID/time/digest audit remains; no other deletion endpoint exists.

cases.name: Native release qualification evidence
preconditions: Target implementation built from the pinned specification revision.
Fixtures and fault controls named by the case are available and hashed.
steps: Execute all RUN cases against pinned commit/fixtures on each named profile and static absence case; retain raw evidence and environment identity.
expected: Each profile has an independent result per applicable case with hashes/versions/timestamps; NOT_RUN remains until execution; no speed, quality or unsupported-platform claim is recorded.

cases.name: Bounded preflight child and diagnostic receipts
preconditions: Installed candidate with isolated storage and process ownership instrumentation.
steps: Observe fixed preflight child invocation; induce timeout, excess stdout and wrong dependency version.
Save prescribed width 63/heads 4 diagnostic and failed tampered-bundle job receipt.
Try valid/different invalid request, successful job and stale job ID; replay identical idempotency key.
expected: API process imports no ML libraries and performs only service-owned storage checks; child bounds enforced.
Only named negative cases create one diagnostic artifact, no extra job or protected registry mutation; invalid receipt inputs rejected.
Repeated idempotent submission returns same receipt identity.

cases.name: Owner-only control channel
preconditions: Target implementation built from the pinned specification revision.
A second OS user account exists on the qualification machine.
steps: Inspect runtime/control.sock (WSL) or the \\.\pipe\llm-foundations-<instance_id> DACL (Windows).
Run connect, status, request, cancel, events and verify-e01-workspace as the owner; repeat each from the second OS user and from a browser page.
Send a control request with a wrong control_secret, a 1 MiB + 1 byte line, two lines, and an unknown operation.
expected: Socket mode 0600 in a 0700 directory, or a pipe DACL granting only the current user SID plus SYSTEM/Administrators; no TCP listener other than 127.0.0.1:8765 exists.
Owner operations succeed with one canonical JSON response line; other-user and browser attempts cannot connect.
Wrong secret, oversize, multi-line and unknown operations return {"ok":false,"error":{...}} with AUTH_REQUIRED, PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE, INVALID_REQUEST, INVALID_REQUEST respectively and change no state.

cases.name: Malformed event and list cursor matrix
preconditions: Target implementation built from the pinned specification revision.
A paired session and a completed job with exactly 3 events exist; two list pages of jobs exist.
steps: Freeze subchecks AC-RUN-022.<endpoint>.<value> for endpoints /events and /event-stream and after_cursor values abc, -1, 1.5, 2147483648, empty, 0, 3 (= last_cursor), 4 (= last_cursor + 1) and 2147483647; record registry revision, job, event and idempotency row counts.
Send each value to both endpoints.

On GET /jobs, /artifacts and /notes send cursor empty, a cursor issued under a different state filter, a cursor with one byte changed, a 200-character random string and a cursor issued before a service restart with a new instance_id.
expected: abc, -1, 1.5, 2147483648 and empty after_cursor return 400 VALIDATION_FAILED reason SCHEMA_INVALID with field_path after_cursor on both endpoints, and the stream sends no text/event-stream bytes.
0 returns cursors 1-3; 3 returns items [] with has_more false and next_after_cursor 3; 4 and 2147483647 return 400 VALIDATION_FAILED reason SEMANTIC_INVALID at after_cursor.
An empty list cursor returns the first page; every other malformed or foreign list cursor returns 400 VALIDATION_FAILED reason SEMANTIC_INVALID with field_path cursor.
Registry revision, job, event and idempotency row counts are unchanged after every rejected request.

cases.name: JSON scalar substitution matrix
preconditions: Target implementation built from the pinned specification revision.
A paired session exists; for each JSON request body in openapi.json (including the dataset metadata part) a valid fixture request exists.
steps: Enumerate every scalar member reachable in each JSON request-body schema (array items at index 0) and freeze subchecks AC-RUN-023.<component>.<pointer>.<substitution> using exactly these substitutions by member type. string or enum member: number 1, true, [], {}. integer member: "50", true, 1.0, 1e0, [], {}. number member: "1.5", true, [], {}. boolean member: "true", 1, [], {}. Every required non-nullable member additionally: null.
Record registry revision, job, event and idempotency row counts; send each substituted request with a fresh Idempotency-Key where required.
expected: Every subcheck returns 400 VALIDATION_FAILED with reason SCHEMA_INVALID, or the x-reason-code of the failing subschema when every failing keyword lies inside one, and a field error whose field_path is the substituted member's JSON Pointer.
No job, accepted-state event, idempotency row, artifact, note, evidence or registry revision is created or changed by any subcheck.

cases.name: CUDA preflight decides GPU support by the fixed rule
preconditions: A test double supplies the launcher's GPU query result and the child's device count, compute capability, compiled architecture list, memory and matrix difference; the table rows need no GPU.

The passing base row is: query line 'NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070, 12.0, 616.92, 12227'; one device; capability 12.0; the cu128 Linux list sm_70 to sm_120; total 12,227 MiB; free 11,000 MiB; difference 2e-7.
steps: Starting from the base row, change one value per row: the GPU query is missing, exits 9, or prints no four-field line; driver 572.60 and 572.61; compute capability 7.0 and 7.5; capability 8.9 against a list containing 8.6 but not 8.9; capability 12.0 against the cu126 list 5.0 to 9.0; total memory 3,583 and 3,584 MiB; free memory 2,047 and 2,048 MiB; relative difference 1.1e-5 and 1e-5.
Run a row that fails both the driver and the capability rule.
Launch with an explicit CUDA profile and a failing row.
expected: The rows give, in order: CUDA_DEVICE_NOT_FOUND three times; CUDA_DRIVER_TOO_OLD then pass; CUDA_CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED then pass; pass; CUDA_ARCH_NOT_IN_BUILD; CUDA_MEMORY_INSUFFICIENT then pass; CUDA_MEMORY_INSUFFICIENT then pass; CUDA_NUMERIC_CHECK_FAILED then pass. The base row passes.
The first failing step in RUN-015 order decides: CUDA_DRIVER_TOO_OLD.
P00-RUN-002-PROFILE fails with the reason code in its observed text; the receipt's cuda object has result failed and that reason_code; no root lock is published; no job or CPU fallback occurs.

cases.name: Startup selects the environment's profile and offers a supported GPU without switching
preconditions: An install directory holds envs/<OS CPU profile> and, for the GPU rows, envs/<OS CUDA profile>.
A GPU query test double returns, in turn: no executable; 'NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070, 12.0, 616.92, 12227'; driver 572.60; compute capability 6.1; memory 2,048 MiB.
steps: Run gpu-check from the CPU environment for each query result, with and without the CUDA environment present.
Start serve without --profile from the CPU environment, then from the CUDA environment; start each environment with the other build's --profile explicitly.
From the CUDA environment, start serve with a failing CUDA preflight row from AC-RUN-024.
Read GET /api/v1/runtime from each instance that started, and run one tiny_train job on it.
expected: gpu-check prints one GpuOffer JSON line with status not_detected, available, unsupported CUDA_DRIVER_TOO_OLD, unsupported CUDA_CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED and unsupported CUDA_MEMORY_INSUFFICIENT respectively, then the fixed RUN-001 sentence for that status and environment state, and exits 0 without importing Torch.

Without --profile the CPU environment starts the OS CPU profile and the CUDA environment starts the OS CUDA profile; an explicit profile that does not match the environment's Torch build fails before the lock with BACKEND_VERSION_MISMATCH.
The failing CUDA start prints the reason code, its meaning and the CPU launch command, publishes no lock and starts no CPU instance.

gpu_offer is in_use on the CUDA instance and available on the CPU instance when the query line passes, with cuda_environment_installed and explicit_profile matching the launch; each job's device equals the instance profile's device.
